Implement a robust DIMACS CNF parser in COBOL: supports c comments, p cnf <vars> <clauses>, arbitrary whitespace, multiple lines per clause, and 0 clause terminators.

{"replace_all": false, "file_path": "/Users/mathieuacher/SANDBOX/SATCobol-cc/tests/run_tests.sh", "old_string": "# Negative case: missing file should exit non-zero.", "new_string": "# --solve: known SAT instances, then verify the produced model.
run_solve_sat() {
    local name="$1"
    local cnf="$2"
    local out_file
    out_file="$(mktemp -t cobsat-model.XXXXXX)"
    "$BIN" --solve "$cnf" >"$out_file" 2>/dev/null
    local first
    first="$(head -1 "$out_file")"
    if [ "$first" != "s SATISFIABLE" ]; then
        fail=$((fail+1))
        failures+=("$name: solver did not report SATISFIABLE (got: $first)")
        echo "FAIL $name (got: $first)"
        rm -f "$out_file"
        return
    fi
    if "$BIN" --check-model "$cnf" "$out_file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        pass=$((pass+1))
        echo "ok   $name"
    else
        fail=$((fail+1))
        failures+=("$name: model rejected by --check-model")
        echo "FAIL $name (model rejected)"
        cat "$out_file" | sed 's/^/     /'
    fi
    rm -f "$out_file"
}

# --solve: known UNSAT instances must report s UNSATISFIABLE.
run_solve_unsat() {
    local name="$1"
    local cnf="$2"
    local out
    out="$("$BIN" --solve "$cnf" 2>/dev/null)"
    local first
    first="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | head -1)"
    if [ "$first" = "s UNSATISFIABLE" ]; then
        pass=$((pass+1))
        echo "ok   $name"
    else
        fail=$((fail+1))
        failures+=("$name: expected UNSATISFIABLE, got: $first")
        echo "FAIL $name (got: $first)"
    fi
}
